## August 2026 US total vehicle sales (FRED TOTALNSA): research brief

### 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on FRED series TOTALNSA (BEA Total Vehicle Sales, not seasonally adjusted, in thousands of units). This counts light vehicles plus heavy trucks, so it usually comes in about 40-50k above the light-vehicle unit totals that Cox and NADA report. [FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/TOTALNSA)
- 2026-07-01 observation: the latest value is 1402.98 for July 2026, per the code baseline from FRED. [FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/data/TOTALNSA.txt)
- Recent monthly values for 2026: Jan 1116.7, Feb 1206.3, Mar 1430.9, Apr 1421.9, May 1522.6, Jun 1423.1, Jul about 1403. [FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/data/TOTALNSA.txt)

### 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. As of 2026-08-14 the month is only half over. BEA usually publishes in the first days of the following month, consistent with resolution around 2026-09-04.

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-07: NADA's Market Beat (Omdia data) put the July SAAR at 16.33M, down 1.4% from a year earlier. That ended a two-month run of year-over-year gains that started in May (+3.1%). July came in below forecasts. NADA kept its full-year 2026 forecast at 16.0M. [CollisionWeek](https://collisionweek.com/2026/08/07/new-light-vehicle-sales-slip-1-4-july-ending-two-month-run-gains/), [NADA](https://www.nada.org/media/20028/download)
- Early Aug 2026: Cox's initial estimate for July was about 1.36M light vehicles at a 16.3M SAAR. The January-July SAAR averaged about 16.0M, down 2.2% year over year. [Cox](https://www.coxautoinc.com/insights/cox-automotive-forecast-july-2026-u-s-auto-sales-forecast/), [Mercer Capital](https://mercercapital.com/insights/blogs/auto-dealer-valuation-insights-blog/2026/july-2026-saar/)
- Late Jul 2026: forecasts made before the July data were higher than the result: J.D. Power/GlobalData about 16.9M, Cox about 16.7M (it would have been the strongest pace of 2026). [J.D. Power](https://www.jdpower.com/business/press-releases/jd-power-globaldata-automotive-forecast-july-2026/), [CollisionWeek](https://collisionweek.com/2026/07/27/july-new-vehicle-sales-pace-highest-selling-rate-2026/)
- Calendar (my own count): August 2026 has 26 selling days, with 5 Sundays and Labor Day falling on Sept 7. August 2025 probably had one more industry selling day. Cox credited that August with one extra selling day compared with July. [Cox Aug 2025](https://www.coxautoinc.com/insights-hub/cox-automotive-forecast-august-2025-u-s-auto-sales-forecast/)

### 4. Base rates and seasonality
How the series moved from July to August (FRED TOTALNSA):

| Year | July | August | Aug/Jul | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2021 | 1316.7 | 1129.0 | 0.857 | chip shortage |
| 2022 | 1164.7 | 1178.1 | 1.011 | |
| 2023 | 1339.9 | 1365.0 | 1.019 | |
| 2024 | 1328.9 | 1457.2 | 1.096 | |
| 2025 | 1425.7 | 1500.4 | 1.052 | boosted by buyers rushing before the EV tax credit expired on 2025-09-30, plus the extra selling day |

Sources: [FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/data/TOTALNSA.txt), [Cox Aug 2025](https://www.coxautoinc.com/insights-hub/cox-automotive-forecast-august-2025-u-s-auto-sales-forecast/)

- Applying the 2022-2025 ratios to July 2026 (1403) gives about 1418, 1430, 1538 and 1476.
- 2026 compared with past years: July 2026 (1403) was 1.6% below July 2025 (1426). The SAAR pace is roughly flat to slightly down from a year earlier, at about 16.0-16.3M against 16.1M in August 2025.
- August 2025 (1500) is probably an inflated comparison because of the EV rush and the extra selling day.
- The statistical baseline's interquartile range for one-month changes is 1291 to 1573, with a median of 1415.

### 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on this series.
- I found no August 2026 forecast from Cox, J.D. Power/GlobalData or S&P published on or before 2026-08-14. These usually come out around August 20-27, after the question closes.

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Around Aug 20-27: J.D. Power/GlobalData and Cox August forecasts (after the close).
- Around Sept 1-3: automakers report August sales, Wards/Omdia release the SAAR, then BEA/FRED publish TOTALNSA.
- Things that could move August: the Labor Day weekend promotions (Labor Day is in September this year, so less of that weekend falls in August than in some years), tariff-related pricing, incentive levels, and the high-teens average transaction prices (about $45-50k).
- This series does not depend on the weather.

**Bottom line:** I found nothing that settles the question before it closes. July 2026 was about 1403, and recent August/July ratios have run between 1.01 and 1.10. August 2026 has a soft comparison problem: one fewer selling day than August 2025 and no EV-credit rush.
